title: Infrastructure Software Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Role Description

As an Infrastructure Engineer, your role will be crucial in shaping and constructing the robust systems that not only support our current flagship products but also lay the groundwork for the next wave of engineering innovations. From optimizing user experiences across various projects to ensuring seamless scalability and data integrity, you'll be at the forefront of shaping the technological backbone of our platform.

Collaborating closely with cross-functional teams, you'll leverage your expertise to tackle audacious challenges and push the boundaries of what's possible. Your contributions will directly impact millions of users, as every line of code you write furthers our mission to revolutionize the way people work and collaborate.

Join us in redefining the future, where your passion for building scalable, reliable systems will drive meaningful change on a global scale.

Our Engineering Career Framework is viewable by anyone outside the company and describes what’s expected for our engineers at each of our career levels. Check out our blog post on this topic and more here.

Responsibilities

  • Build infrastructure capable of managing metadata for hundreds of billions of files, handling hundreds of petabytes of user data, and facilitating millions of concurrent connections.
  • Assist in expanding Dropbox's role as the data-fabric, linking hundreds of millions of applications, devices, and services worldwide, while spearheading efforts to improve interoperability and adaptability across various ecosystems.
  • Measure and optimize Dropbox's analytics platform to maintain its status as one of the most advanced in the industry for extracting meaningful insights from vast data volumes.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to innovate and implement solutions that enhance the performance, reliability, and security of Dropbox's infrastructure, ensuring a seamless experience for users worldwide.

On-call work may be necessary occasionally to help address bugs, outages, or other operational issues, with the goal of maintaining a stable and high-quality experience for our customers.

Requirements

  • BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science or related technical field involving coding (e.g., physics or mathematics), or equivalent technical experience
  • 5+ years of professional software development experience
  • Demonstrated experience in building and managing large-scale, multi-threaded, and geographically distributed backend systems
  • Proficient in programming and debugging across a range of languages such as Python, Go, C/C++, or Java
  • Experience working with operating system internals, filesystems, databases, networks, and compilers. 
  • Ability to independently execute tasks at hand

Preferred Qualifications

  • Familiarity with Semaphores and Mutexes

descriptionHtml:
Role Description

We are looking for a data-driven, systems-thinking Sales Operations Manager to own the operating infrastructure that powers our go-to-market engine. In this highly visible Individual Contributor role, you will serve as the backbone of a regional Sales organization and translate go-to-market strategy into an executable operating model.

You will act as the primary regional business partner for sales executives, supporting all routes to market within the region. You will own or coordinate supporting sales planning, territory and quota execution, forecast interpretation, operational improvements, and translation of strategic priorities into clear execution plans.   You’ll drive process clarity, pipeline health, forecasting hygiene, and cross-functional governance, using AI and automation-enabled workflows to reduce manual reporting effort while maintaining strong human judgment over business recommendations. Your top priority each day will be to ensure excellence in execution and reporting on our regional goals. 

Responsibilities

  • Work in close partnership with the Chief Business Officer’s organization and the GTM Strategy & Programs team to connect regional Sales Operations to company-wide priorities, provide timely inputs for executive reporting, and ensure consistency across regional and corporate operating cadences.
  • Lead end-to-end coverage design, including segmentation, book cutting, territory planning, account assignment, capacity planning, and quota allocation in partnership with Sales Leadership, Compensation, Finance, Systems, and Analytics.
  • Own CRM QA and hygiene for the supported region, including SFDC hierarchy management, pipeline quality, process compliance, forecast integrity, deal quality investigations, and exception resolution.
  • Partner with leadership on pipeline inspection, forecasting, and opportunity assessment, and build executive-ready reporting, dashboards, MBR/QBR readouts, and business insights that help leaders identify risks and make better decisions.
  • Partner with Sales Strategy, Systems, Analytics, Compensation, Finance, and Enablement to automate recurring workflows and continuously improve how the team operates.
  • Support organization design, interim coverage plans, role changes, new-hire onboarding, SPIF development and administration, and Channel deal registration as part of the regional operating model.

Requirements

  • Proven experience scaling Sales Operations across Europe, supporting a complex, multi-country sales organization with diverse markets, languages, and evolving go-to-market motions.
  • Professional working proficiency in English is required as this role regularly collaborates with global teams
  • 8+ years of experience in sales operations, business strategy, investment banking, venture capital, private equity, or corporate advisory, or 6 years of experience with an advanced degree.

descriptionHtml:
Role Description

We are seeking a Senior FP&A Partner to help shape and accelerate growth across our core business. This highly visible role will serve as a strategic thought partner to Product leadership, using financial analysis, business insights, and structured problem-solving to influence both near-term priorities and long-term strategy.

The ideal candidate combines strong financial acumen with a deep understanding of SaaS business models and growth drivers. They will translate complex data into clear insights, identify opportunities to improve business performance, and help leaders evaluate investments and strategic tradeoffs. Success in this role requires a self-starter who is comfortable navigating ambiguity, building structure where it does not yet exist, and collaborating across Product, Finance, Data Science, Marketing, and other cross-functional teams.

This individual will also be expected to embrace AI-enabled ways of working, using modern tools to improve the speed, quality, and scalability of financial analysis and decision support.

Responsibilities

  • Serve as a strategic thought partner to Product leadership, helping shape short-term priorities and long-term direction for the core business
  • Build driver-based financial models that connect product performance and customer behavior to revenue, ARR, retention, and profitability
  • Evaluate growth initiatives, product investments, pricing strategies, and resource allocation decisions through rigorous financial and strategic analysis
  • Develop business cases and scenario analyses that clearly articulate expected returns, risks, dependencies, and tradeoffs
  • Partner across Product, Finance, Data Science, and Marketing to establish targets, define success metrics, and evaluate business performance
  • Identify emerging trends, performance gaps, and growth opportunities, translating complex data into clear, actionable recommendations for senior leadership

descriptionHtml:
Role Description

Dropbox is hiring an Integrated Campaign Strategist to architect and orchestrate marketing campaigns for priority product launches and evergreen marketing motions. This role turns business priorities, audience insight, and product positioning into a clear campaign strategy that defines the audience, narrative, journey, channel roles, activation sequence, and measurement plan.

You will be the steward of how these campaigns show up in market across owned, earned, and paid channels. Working across Product Marketing, Brand and Creative, Comms, Web, Lifecycle, Paid Media, Content, Events, Marketing Operations, Analytics, and Sales, you will align teams around one integrated plan, connect individual activations into a coherent enterprise buyer experience, and guide the campaign from brief through launch, optimization, and learning.

This is a senior individual contributor role for a strategist who can lead through influence, make tradeoffs in ambiguity, and balance strong market storytelling with measurable business impact. You will help Dropbox bring important product stories to enterprise audiences with greater consistency, relevance, and effectiveness.

  • Campaign strategy architecture: Translate mid-market and enterprise business goals, product positioning, audience insight, and market context into integrated campaign strategies for key launches and evergreen motions, including objectives, audience, narrative, journey, channel roles, phasing, and measurement.

  • Performance and optimization: Partner with Marketing Data Science and channel owners to define full funnel success measures, synthesize owned, earned, and paid signals, identify what is driving or limiting performance, and recommend changes to audience, narrative, creative, sequencing, or channel mix.
  • Portfolio learning and scale: Capture campaign insights, codify reusable plays, distinguish enduring strategy from launch specific execution, and apply learning across the enterprise campaign portfolio to improve future launches and evergreen motions.

Requirements

  • 8+ years B2B marketing experience in integrated campaigns, enterprise marketing, product marketing activation, brand to demand, or a related discipline, ideally in SaaS or technology.
  • Direct experience building out campaign strategy and accountable to the outcome (pipeline generation, revenue generation).
  • Demonstrated ownership of complex integrated campaigns from strategy and brief through activation, optimization, and post campaign learning.
  • Strong campaign architecture skills, including audience definition, narrative development, buyer journey design, channel planning, phasing, and measurement.
  • Experience orchestrating owned, earned, and paid programs and understanding the distinct role each plays in building awareness, consideration, demand, and customer growth.
  • Ability to translate product positioning and enterprise customer insight into a cohesive market story and connected audience experience across multiple teams and touchpoints.
  • Strong cross functional leadership and program judgment, including the ability to establish decision rights, navigate competing priorities, resolve dependencies, and influence without direct authority.
  • Analytical fluency and experience using campaign, brand, engagement, and revenue signals to evaluate performance, communicate impact, and make optimization decisions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading enterprise product launch campaigns and building evergreen motions for a multi product B2B portfolio.
  • Experience partnering closely with Corporate Communications, analyst relations, customer advocacy, or social teams to connect earned programs with owned and paid activation.
  • Experience marketing to complex enterprise buying groups across industries, company sizes, regions, or stages of maturity.
  • Familiarity with marketing automation, CRM, media, intent, experimentation, and attribution platforms used to activate and measure integrated campaigns.

title: Senior Corporate Enterprise Platform Engineer, Windows
descriptionHtml:
Role Description

As a Senior Client Platform Engineer on CorpFleet Engineering, you will own and improve Dropbox’s Windows endpoint platform. You will bring deep Windows and Intune expertise, make patching and application delivery more reliable, and build automation that reduces recurring work for the team.

This is a hands-on role combining Windows technical ownership with the development of a more code-managed endpoint platform. You will help evaluate and adopt FleetDM, osquery, infrastructure-as-code, and GitOps practices where they improve reliability, visibility, and maintainability. You will strengthen the current environment while building and validating the path forward—not assume that replacing a tool is the answer.

You will work with CorpInfra, IAM, Security, and support teams to make practical technical decisions, lead multi-phase improvements, and clarify ownership. You will also mentor teammates through pairing, code review, and shared operational practices. This is an individual-contributor role, not a people-management position.

Responsibilities

  • Own endpoint reliability and lifecycle management. Improve provisioning, application delivery, updates, security configuration, and troubleshooting across the endpoint environment.
  • Make patching predictable and safe. Strengthen update workflows through testing, controlled rollouts, and remediation.
  • Make fleet health trustworthy and actionable. Improve reporting on device health, patching, and configuration, with clear ownership for resolving issues.
  • Build maintainable automation. Turn recurring work into reliable, tested workflows that other engineers can operate.
  • Advance code-managed endpoint operations. Adopt tools and practices that improve configuration management, validation, and deployment.
  • Lead cross-functional platform improvements. Define practical roadmaps, resolve dependencies, and balance security, reliability, employee experience, and team capacity.
  • Strengthen the team’s capability. Mentor teammates, review code and designs, and document reusable practices that improve coverage across the endpoint team.

Requirements

  • Significant experience engineering and operating Windows endpoint environments, with personal ownership beyond ticket handling or routine console administration.
  • Deep hands-on Intune experience across device lifecycle, configuration and compliance policies, application management, update workflows, and relevant Entra ID dependencies.
  • Strong Windows troubleshooting skills across operating-system behavior, services, logs, networking, certificates, identity, and security controls. Able to distinguish reported management status from actual endpoint health.
  • Recent ownership of Windows and third-party application patching, including staged deployment, user-impact validation, failed-device handling, exceptions, and recovery.
  • Strong practical PowerShell skills and familiarity with at least one additional programming language, such as Python, Go, or C#. Experience building and maintaining production automation or systems integrations.
  • Demonstrated use of version control, code review, automated checks, and controlled deployment for operational changes. Able to explain safe retries, failure handling, secrets management, and configuration drift.
  • Ability to independently define and deliver multi-phase work, prioritize under ambiguity, partner across teams, and mentor other engineers.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including concise technical decisions, incident updates, runbooks, and effective asynchronous collaboration.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Production experience with FleetDM on Windows, including agent operations, policies, queries, targeting, API integrations, or configuration managed through GitOps.
  • Practical osquery and SQL experience for endpoint inventory, health, or security use cases, including query validation, performance considerations, and handling stale or missing results.
  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code or declarative configuration, continuous integration and delivery, and migration or coexistence between endpoint-management platforms.
  • Experience with Automox, Patch My PC, or comparable tools, and with endpoint privilege management, application control, encryption, or other security controls.
  • Experience supporting developer-heavy, distributed environments and contributing reusable automation across Windows, macOS, or Linux.

title: Executive Assistant to the Chief Business Officer
descriptionHtml:
Role Description

As the Executive Business Partner to Dropbox’s Chief Business Officer, you’ll create leverage through exceptional executive administration, judgment, and follow-through. You’ll own the details that help him and his team operate at its best: a strategic calendar, seamless travel, useful meetings, clear preparation, accurate communications, and thoughtful coordination across the Chief Business Officer’s team and the broader Dropbox leadership system.

This is a high-impact executive administration role in a fast-moving and evolving business. You’ll work closely with the CBO, his Chief of Staff, the Office of the CBO team, other executive admins, Chiefs of Staff, business partners, and senior cross-functional leaders. You’ll often need to make decisions with incomplete information, surface risks early, and keep work moving without creating unnecessary noise or rework.

This is an exceptional administration role where you’ll bring judgment and a point of view, but your primary responsibility is to make the executive and the operating system work better through accurate, proactive, collaborative execution. You’ll first learn the existing system, build trust, and develop pattern recognition — then you’ll bring best practices and your expertise to help reshape systems and make them work even better.

If you’re highly organized, calm under pressure, direct in your communication, persistent about follow through, and energized by making complex executive work feel simple, then this role is for you.

Responsibilities

  • Own a complex calendar as a strategic operating tool, balancing executive priorities, customer and revenue commitments, leadership forums, preparation time, focus time, travel, and personal commitments
  • Support meeting prep by ensuring the right attendees, context, agendas, pre-reads, links, decision points, and follow-up actions are in place
  • Coordinate domestic and international travel end-to-end, including itineraries, ground transportation, hotel and meeting logistics, time-zone planning, contingency plans, and preparation or recovery time
  • Partner with the CBO’s Chief of Staff to maintain shared visibility into priorities, risks, requests, decisions, and follow-ups
  • Collaborate with other executive admins, Chiefs of Staff, business partners, and cross-functional leaders to resolve scheduling and operating needs without creating parallel processes or confusion
  • Support communication by tracking drafts, deadlines, approvals, distribution lists, links, and follow-through, ensuring that important messages are accurate and do not stall
  • Plan and execute executive meetings, offsites, and leadership events with strong attention to detail and a crisp focus on attendee experience, budget, and contingency planning
  • Maintain accurate administrative systems, including expenses, contacts, recurring meeting structures, action-item tracking, and relevant executive reference materials
  • Surface risks early, make recommendations, and own issues through resolution rather than simply completing the first task requested

Requirements

  • 8+ years of experience supporting a senior executive, preferably a C-level executive or equivalent leader in a complex, fast-moving organization
  • Expertise managing a highly complex executive calendar across multiple time zones, competing priorities, recurring leadership forums, customer commitments, and protected personal or focus time
  • Experience planning complex domestic and international travel, including contingency planning and coordination across multiple travelers, hosts, vendors, and time zones
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate directly, concisely, and appropriately with senior leaders and cross-functional partners
  • Experience working with and/or for a senior Chief of Staff in tight, trusted partnership on systems- and process-based approaches to make order out of competing priorities
  • Proven ability to prioritize independently, make sound decisions with incomplete information, and escalate risks early with a recommendation
  • Demonstrated track record of accurate, detail-oriented execution across scheduling, events, communications, expenses, and follow-through
  • Experience working as part of an admin community and collaborating across executive offices rather than operating as an isolated support partner
  • Comfort working in a high-change environment where priorities shift quickly and the person must continuously re-plan without losing important details
  • High competency with workplace systems, including Slack, Gmail, Concur, Navan, Google Docs (and of course Dropbox!), as well as AI tooling for efficiency through human-machine partnership
  • Ability to work primarily on Eastern Time, with flexibility for occasional EMEA and APJ commitments and executive travel
